scope: Same-process native Unity editor Mono comparison of the previous C# adaptation and the updated C# adaptation; not native C++ or player timing.

provenance.sourceAssembly: A and B plus identical helper bodies compiled together into a fresh ephemeral assembly per case; source hashes are emitted by the entry point.

arms.C: Array.Sort for Array; List.Sort for List

method.warmup: Each arm warmed for at least 100 ms of accumulated sorting time; warmup batches doubled until at least 20 ms, bounded by a 128 MiB replica payload budget.
method.measurement: One Stopwatch interval wraps all prepared replica sorts in a slot. Preparation, comparer construction, cloning, and validation of every replica are outside timing. Every arm uses the same replication count in each case, targeted at 40 ms for the fastest warmed arm; observed minimumSlotMs governs the clock floor.
method.validation: Every integer replica exactly equals Array.Sort output. Historical wide replicas checked sorted expected keys, uniqueness after narrowing identity to Int32, and fields3,4,5; they did not independently prove the full64-bit identity range or key-to-original-tuple association. Complete wide value/permutation behavior is separately covered by the real NUnit regressions; these historical timing measurements must not claim the stronger per-replica tuple guarantee.

bootstrap.unit: Paired eight-slot A/B batch; resample eight complete batches with replacement, preserving within-batch pairing.
bootstrap.statistic: Median B / median A over all resampled slots

method.allocation: No native allocation claim: the allocating positive control for GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread returned zero on this editor.
method.limitations: Editor results include generic comparer and CLR costs and do not establish IL2CPP, target-player, native-C++, allocation, or universal-speedup claims. Wide E738 compact-index cases and Noise1 are observed regressions.
method.listWriteBackLimitation: The generated source clones use an identical indexer-loop WriteBack shim for List<T>, rather than production IListBulk.cs Clear/AddRange replacement. List cells compare those clones and do not measure the exact production List backend; array cells do not use this shim.

routeDiagnostics.note: Separate same-source instrumentation used overlapping ascending runs, growing descending-pile pressure, and eight sampled windows with three adjacent inversions each. Disjoint Runs33/38/39 timing inputs use the global natural-run path; OverlapRuns33/38/39 are the outer-run stress shapes. The original wide diagnostic narrowed identity to Int32 and checked fields3/5, so it did not independently prove whole-tuple association; stronger raw diagnostics and final per-replica validation are retained separately.
routeDiagnostics.wideValidationSubset: Sorted keys, narrowed Int32 identity uniqueness, Item3 complement, Item5 payload; not complete64-bit identity/key association.

reproduction.note: The checked-in replay templates add license headers, formatting, and a separate nested-comparer source file. Historical wide controls used weaker validation as described in their record; replay uses complete tuple association checks. Template hashes identify the original measured templates, not the subsequently packaged replay files.
reproduction.listWriteBackLimitation: The generated source clones use an identical indexer-loop WriteBack shim for List<T>, rather than production IListBulk.cs Clear/AddRange replacement. List cells compare those clones and do not measure the exact production List backend; array cells do not use this shim.
